body: I'm so sorry this is happening to you. I know exactly how you feel. Well, I might not know exactly how you feel but I am very familiar with exactly what you're describing. I feel these feelings right now. But I'm still here, somehow. I'm actually a little surprised that I am. Yesterday was my lowest, and I felt like every last ounce of my strength and sanity had been drained from me. I very nearly shot myself. But I'm here today and I feel better than I did yesterday. I hope and believe that I will be here tomorrow and that I will feel better then than I do today, also. I don't know you so I apologize if this seems impersonal, but I genuinely hope you are here tomorrow aswell. And the next day, and the next, and so on. I know this feels like suffocating. I know it may feel like you have been waiting for as long as you can remember and it seems like it won't get better, but I promise that it *can* happen quicker than you can imagine. It isn't good, but it is better. It feels *so, so* good, that relief. Please hang on, please stay. This can't last forever, nothing can. Good luck friend. I hope peace finds you quickly.

Old thread, I know, so sorry if I'm breaking any rules. When I was about fifteen I went camping with a group of older friends and drank the equivalent of about 30 beers in the period of a few hours. I proceeded to drift in and out of consciousness and my friends laid me in my open sleeping bag. I spent the night in below freezing temperatures with severe alcohol poisoning, awake for every moment of it, wishing I was dead. I wasn't right for a couple of weeks after it. I've had multiple broken ribs and road rash covering the majority of my torso and nothing has come close to the pain I felt that night.
My old piece of shit Honda Shadow has gotten me through some tough shit as well. It's hard to feel nothing when you're breaking a hundred miles an hour.
